'''Shmuel "Mula" Shtrikman''' ({{langx|he|שמואל שטריקמן}}; 21 October 1930 to 11 November 2003) was an Israeli physicist, and a professor at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. Winner of the [[Israel Prize]] for Research in Physics in 2003.<ref name=doyle>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Doyle | first1 = Bill
 | last2 = Treves | first2 = David
 | last3 = Flanders | first3 = Phil
 | last4 = Schultz | first4 = Shelly
 | last5 = Friedlaender | first5 = Fritz
 | last6 = Thomas | first6 = Harry
 | title = In Memoriam: Shmuel (Mula) Shtrikman (1930–2003)
 | journal =  IEEE Transactions on Magnetics
 | volume = 40
 | issue = 6
 | pages = 3441–3442
 | date = 6 November 2004
 | doi = 10.1109/TMAG.2004.837391
}}</ref>

==Biography==
Born in [[Brest, Belarus]] (then Poland) to Abraham and Esther Shtrikman, sister of Sapir and brother of biochemist [[Nathan Sharon]]. Shtrikman immigrated to Israel with his family in 1934. In the first year the family lived in [[Kfar Saba]]; a year later they moved to [[Tel Aviv]]. In the [[1948 Arab–Israeli War]] he served in the Air Force.<ref name=hayadan>{{cite web
 | title = נפטר פרופ שמואל (מולה) שטריקמן, חתן פרס ישראל בחקר הפיסיקה
 | website = www.hayadan.org.il
 | publisher = Hayadan
 | date = 21 November 2003
 | url = http://www.hayadan.org.il/shtrickman
 | access-date = 17 May 2016}}</ref>

Shtrikman began his studies at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] in 1950. After graduation with a BSc in 1954, he joined the Department of Electronics at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], where he did his doctoral degree in Electrical Engineering, received in 1958. In 1967 he was appointed professor at the Weizmann Institute. In 1981 to 1982 he served as head of the department of the Electronic Physics Institute. In 1994 he was elected to the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref name=hayadan />

His research concerned various fields of physics: the behaviour of particles under the influence of a magnetic field; liquid crystals; [[multicritical point|Lifshitz points]]; [[composite material|composites]] constructed from inhomogeneous distributions of ingredients; and calculating the elasticity of composite materials. His 1963 work with [[Zvi Hashin]] on the application of [[Calculus of variations|variational]] approach on the [[Linear elasticity|elastic]] behaviour of multiphase materials<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Hashin | first1 = Zvi
 | author1-link = Zvi Hashin
 | last2 = Shtrikman | first2 = Shmuel
 | author2-link = Shmuel Shtrikman
 | title = A variational approach to the theory of the elastic behaviour of multiphase materials
 | journal = Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
 | publisher = Elsevier
 | volume = 11
 | issue = 2
 | pages = 127–140
 | doi = 10.1016/0022-5096(63)90060-7
 | year = 1963
 | bibcode = 1963JMPSo..11..127H
 }}</ref> was influential on the theory of [[Effective medium approximations|effective media]] and composites; the upper and lower-bounds for attainable effective constitutive parameters derived in this work are known as Hashin—Shtrikman bounds.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Watt |first1=J. Peter |title=Hashin‐Shtrikman bounds on the effective elastic moduli of polycrystals with orthorhombic symmetry |journal=[[Journal of Applied Physics]] |date=1979 |volume=50 |pages=6290–6295 |doi=10.1063/1.325768}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last = Sihvola | first = Ari | date = 1999 | title = Electromagnetic Mixing Formulas and Applications | publisher = The Institution of Engineering and Technology | series = IEE Electromagnetic Waves Series 47 | location = London | isbn = 978-0-85296-772-0}}</ref>

==Awards==
Shtrikman received the following awards:<ref name=doyle />
* [[Weizmann Institute of Science|Weizmann]] Prize for Science (1968)
* Michael Landau Prize (1975)
* [[IEEE Magnetics Society]] Distinguished Lecturer (1984 and 1997–1998)
* [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev|Ben Gurion University]] Applied Electronics Prize (1988)
* R. M. Burton Award by the Weizmann Institute Foundation (1988)
* [[Israel Prize]] in Physics (2003)
* [[Israel Defense Prize]] (1979 and 1987)
